text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2. p99 jumped from 420ms -> 2.8s over the last 5m. Paging eng-oncall.

sara: paging oncall — seeing customers start to complain about streaming stalls. p95 up ~600ms, p99 sustained ~2.8s. traces show stalls at kv-cache access in cont-batch path.

mike: oncall here. joining. can you paste the short graph and a couple of example request ids?

sara: put basic numbers in case useful: overall error rate unchanged, but 5xx tail up 0.6% concentrated on streaming path. impact at peak: ~3.1% of active streams experiencing >1s stalls. sample req ids: rQf7, rQf8, rQa1.

anita: grabbing traces now. looks like a pattern: long stall during packer->kv lookup when mixed sequence lengths present (hot short queries interleaved with long seqs). cont-batcher holds KV cache lock for ~300-900ms on some shards.

ryan: ugh, this smells like the mixed-seqlen packing amplification we saw last quarter. quick question: are we seeing a scheduler fairness regression?

sara: yes, scheduler metrics indicate shifted fairness weight toward packers handling long-seq traffic after yesterday's deploy. config `batcher.scheduler_policy=throughput_prefer_long` applied in us-west-2.

mike: ok first mitigation plan: 1) temporarily flip scheduler back to `fair_share` 2) reduce cont-batch max_pack_size to 8 3) route heavy streaming traffic to dedicated-stream-1 pool for 10m window. can infra run the router change?

kate: infra-bot running router change now. applying route rule: `if path contains /v1/streaming then prefer pool dedicated-stream-1, fallback=hosted`. ETA ~45s.

infra-bot: router update queued. config diff: `+ prefer_pool: dedicated-stream-1 (weight 90) - prefer_pool: default-hosted (weight 100)`

anita: flipping scheduler to fair_share on packer nodes (usw2-batcher-*) now. running command on one node to test:

```bash
ssh batcher@usw2-batcher-03
sudo /srv/batcher/bin/batcherctl set scheduler_policy fair_share
sudo /srv/batcher/bin/batcherctl set max_pack_size 8
```

mike: good. while that's rolling, please enable pack_shed=true on streaming route to shed oversized packs if latency overshoots. that's quick config: `redwood route update streaming --pack_shed=true --shed_threshold_ms=500`

sara: done: `route streaming updated: pack_shed=true shed_threshold_ms=500` (applied to us-west-2).

anita: observed immediate reduction in tail on the test batcher node — p99 dropped to ~1.1s for that shard. continuing rollout.

mike: routing is live and batcher policy flipped across 6 nodes. system p99 down to 860ms after 2m. still seeing stragglers on two racks. planning KV eviction/rehash on those nodes next.

ryan: before we kill anything, let's try a targeted KV cache rotation: `kvctl evict --shard s23 --window 30s` to force re-population without global flush.

anita: running kv rotation on s23 and s24 now. watch for transient CPU spike.

infra-bot: kvctl evict completed for s23, s24. re-population started.

sara: after kv rotation p99 stabilized at ~480ms across the cluster. streaming stalls mostly cleared. customer-facing impact appears to have returned to baseline.

mike: summary of mitigations performed: 1) router shifted streaming traffic to dedicated pool 2) scheduler policy -> fair_share 3) max_pack_size reduced to 8 4) pack_shed enabled on route 5) targeted kv evict on two hot shards.

kate: we should run a short canary to validate throughput isn't catastrophically impacted — dedicated-stream-1 capacity is limited. rolling a rate cap: `route streaming set rate_limit=0.9x` to avoid overload.

anita: canary looks ok; throughput down ~5% but latency now within SLO. open item: need follow-up to tune scheduler weighting to avoid repeat after rollback.

sara: customer impact notes for postmortem: - Duration: ~09:42 - 10:06 UTC (24m) - Affected endpoints: /v1/streaming/generate - Symptom: p99 spike to 2.8s, p95 to ~600ms, intermittent streaming stalls - Customers with long-running streams saw stalls ~3% of active streams at peak - Root cause (initial): scheduler policy change + mixed sequence length packing causing KV cache contention and pack amplification.

mike: immediate action items assigned: - anita: write postmortem draft with traces and safe rollback steps (due EOD) - infra: add router automation to fallback sooner if p99>1s for 2m - eng-runtime: add guard to prevent `throughput_prefer_long` from being set globally (config gating)

ryan: long-term work: scheduler QE to add seqlen-aware priority bucketing, packer KV lock sharding, more aggressive targeted cache eviction heuristics.

kate: I'll notify customer success + ops to send proactive messages to customers who reported stalls. draft status: short note + timeline.

sara: good. closing pager. will keep watch on metrics for 30m. :white_check_mark: 

mike: if anything regresses, re-open this thread and ping @pager. otherwise we'll convert to a postmortem channel thread later. thanks team. :heart:
